reasons: The opinion says the search violated the Constitution because there were no reasons to suspect danger or concealment in underwear.

The opinion states the content of the suspicion failed to match the degree of intrusion and later requires suspicion of danger or resort to underwear before moving from outer clothes/backpacks to exposure of intimate parts.
The opinion holds qualified immunity was warranted because lower courts had reached divergent conclusions and the right was not sufficiently clear.
residual_risks: The holding compresses a fact-specific school-search rule into a concise summary.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum precision, phrase the rule as applying to a school strip search exposing intimate parts, rather than to strip searches generally.
